C-FIX-MUSIC-START-RACE.IntentSummary: Close the start race in the music channel, make starting idempotent, and keep the track's position across foreground changes, with tests that pin each behaviour.

MustPassCommand.Command: grep -q 'Future<void> pause' lib/services/music_player.dart && grep -q 'Future<void> resume' lib/services/music_player.dart
grep -q 'one player' test/music_service_test.dart && grep -q 'does not restart' test/music_service_test.dart

T-001.Title: Share the pending player load and add pause to the seam

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The player map holds futures rather than finished players, so concurrent callers for one asset await the same creation and only one AudioPlayer is ever built.
A failed load is dropped from the map, so a later attempt can retry instead of awaiting a broken future forever.
The interface gains pause and resume beside stop, and the implementation maps them to the plugin's own pause and resume.

T-002.Title: Make starting idempotent and keep the position across foreground changes

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Starting a track that is already playing does nothing, so the first resumed notification after registration cannot double playback or restart the track.
Leaving the foreground pauses the track; returning resumes it; neither restarts it.
Switching the channel off still stops and resets, and a finished track still advances the rotation.
The controller tracks what is playing explicitly, rather than inferring it from the life-cycle state.

T-003.Title: Pin the two behaviours that let this through

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A test starts the service twice without awaiting in between and asserts the player was asked for the track exactly once and built exactly one player.
A test sends paused and resumed through the life-cycle hook and asserts the track was neither restarted nor advanced, and that the player was paused and resumed.
The existing four music tests still pass unchanged.

T-004.Title: Record the two scenarios in the durable verification

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: V-M-SOUND gains a scenario stating that concurrent starts yield one player for a track, and one stating that resume continues rather than restarts.
The entry still carries one command covering both audio test files.
